model: TEC26x6(H)-4 and TEC26x6H-4+PIR Fan Coil Thermostat (BACnet MS/TP)
applies_to: Two- or four-pipe fan coils with up to three fan speeds, controlled by the TEC26x6(H)-4 family (on/off, floating or proportional valve outputs, optional dehumidification and PIR occupancy sensing).
summary: The TEC26x6(H)-4 thermostats run fan coils over BACnet MS/TP. The object list covers system mode, fan mode, occupancy command, the six occupied/standby/unoccupied setpoints, loop demands, valve and fan status, alarms and configuration parameters. Humidity and dehumidification objects exist only on the TEC2636 and TEC2656 models; floating valve settings only on the TEC2626 and TEC2636.
notes: Objects from Table 3 on pages 11-17 of the technical bulletin, which also holds separate tables for the other TEC26xx-4 models.
Access comes from the guide's footnotes: read/write, read-only, or writable only after the matching override object is set to Override.
The device object (instance 73aaa, aaa = MS/TP address) is not listed as a point.
Temperatures are listed in °F; the guide also gives the °C range.

source.title: TEC Series BACnet MS/TP Network Temperature and Humidity Controllers Technical Bulletin

integration.summary: Address the thermostat on the BACnet MS/TP trunk, then command System Mode (MV 16) and Occupancy Command (MV 18) and Fan Mode (MV 17) and write the occupied setpoints (AV 39/40). Read Room Temp, Effective Occupancy, Fan Status and the filter and service alarms.

minimum_points.name: System Mode
minimum_points.why: System mode: off, auto, cool or heat

minimum_points.name: Fan Mode
minimum_points.why: Fan mode; states follow Fan Mode Sequence

integration.enable: Occupancy Command (MV 18, 1=Local Occupancy, 2=Occupied, 3=Unoccupied) sets occupancy from the BAS; the first state hands occupancy back to the thermostat. System Mode (MV 16) can switch the unit off.
integration.heartbeat: The guide marks some objects (Room Temp and Fan Status) as possibly releasing on their own after 10 minutes with no BACnet traffic. Keep writing overridden values.
integration.remote_sensors: To feed room temperature from the BAS, set Room Temp Override (BV 8) to Override, then write Room Temp (AV 7). Outdoor Temperature (AV 9) is only valid when it is written over the network.
setup: BACnet MS/TP only. Set the MS/TP address (4 to 127) with the Com addr parameter at the thermostat.
The thermostat names itself TEC26x6-aaa and picks device instance 73aaa, where aaa is the MS/TP address (e.g. 73004). Change either before mapping points if needed.
Leave the thermostat on automatic baud detection; at least one device on the trunk (normally the supervisory controller) needs a fixed baud rate.
Max_Master in the device object is writable.
gotchas: Writing one setpoint of a heating/cooling pair can make the thermostat move the other one to keep the minimum deadband.
Set the configuration parameters before mapping; the guide recommends re-mapping all objects if configuration changes afterwards.
TEC26xx-4 objects do not line up with the older TEC26xx-2 objects; rediscover all points when replacing a -2 thermostat.
Objects with no access mark in the guide are listed here as read-only.
